**Subject:** Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. It has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal, AI visual inspection piloting on its German production line and AI sales forecasting planned for next year. Your stated objective: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Customer data must stay in the EU, and the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, with the date not yet fixed.

**What the Briefing covers for Tamarack Instruments**

We will map the EU AI Act and GDPR to each of the three use cases. These will be framed as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. As a general landscape item rather than a stated Client driver, we will flag United States requirements worth confirming.

The readiness discussion tests the visual inspection pilot against Slow AI, which holds that AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.

We will then show how Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human are put to work through two frameworks:
- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) serves as the board-layer reference. The Briefing supports preparation for ISO/IEC 42001 work but does not confer certification or predict audit outcomes.

We propose to confirm three questions at intake:
- whether works council consultation applies to the visual inspection pilot
- which frameworks the Client already uses
- whether any AI risk events have occurred

**Logistics and price**

The Executive Briefing runs for 2 hours, live virtual, for US$3,000. This sits within the US$80,000 budget approved for this fiscal year. Audience roles are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

**What you receive afterward**

You will receive a follow-up memo covering decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations. Each recommendation is mapped to a next program option with a proposed timeline.

**Next step**

The decision timeline is not yet known. Please reply with a preferred date window, and we will confirm the intake questions and schedule the session.
